summaries: The change introduces a runtime crash due to an off‑by‑one error in the array summation loop.

findings.explanation: The loop boundary was changed from `i < values.length` to `i <= values.length`, causing the loop to access `values[values.length]` on the final iteration. This results in an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` for any non-empty array. For example, calling `ArrayTotals.sum(new int[]{1,2,3})` will throw an exception instead of returning the correct sum of 6.

decisions.reason: The candidate correctly identifies a HIGH severity correctness bug introduced by the change. The loop condition was modified from `i < values.length` to `i <= values.length`, which causes the loop to iterate one time too many. On the final iteration, the code attempts to access `values[values.length]`, which is out of bounds and will throw an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. This is a repeatable crash and a significant correctness issue, as the method will no longer compute the correct sum for any non-empty array.
